title: brew bundle installs the HEY CLI instead of matching the stale hey-desktop cask
description: A leftover 'hey' desktop cask (renamed hey-desktop by Homebrew) answers to the bare token 'hey', so brew bundle says 'Using hey' and never installs basecamp/tap/hey. setup-hey then gives a wrong hint (--enable=packages).
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
- Bootstrap removes the stale hey-desktop record before brew bundle (guarded on no HEY.app)
- setup-hey macOS hint gives a command that works
- command -v hey resolves after bootstrap
close_reason: clear-stale-hey-desktop removed the shadowing cask; brew bundle printed 'Installing hey', HEY agent skill installed

title: Stow skips .DS_Store so Finder litter can't abort the home tree
description: Finder dropped a gitignored .DS_Store in symlinked/home/; stow doesn't ignore it, collides with ~/.DS_Store, and aborts stowing the whole home tree.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
- All stow calls in symlink-dotfiles pass --ignore for .DS_Store
- stow -n home reports no conflicts
close_reason: stow calls now pass --ignore='\.DS_Store' via STOW_IGNORES; dry-run with a planted .DS_Store shows no conflict (vs 1 without)

title: setup-fish checks $SHELL instead of the account login shell
description:
setup-fish (bin/juliet-bootstrap ~L1090) decides whether to chsh from $SHELL. Run from a non-fish parent (e.g. Claude's Bash tool, SHELL=/bin/zsh) it tries chsh even though dscl UserShell is already fish, and chsh fails without a TTY.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Account login shell is fish (dscl . -read ~ UserShell)
2. From a zsh parent (SHELL=/bin/zsh), run juliet-bootstrap -y
3. Bootstrap prints 'Setting fish to default shell...' and chsh fails
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
- Check uses the account login shell (dscl on macOS, getent on Fedora)
- Running bootstrap with SHELL=/bin/zsh skips chsh when the account shell is fish

title: Explain garbled security-step output in juliet-bootstrap
description:
Found via fixme triage of the 2026-10-16 19:06 juliet-bootstrap scrollback. On the first run, the 'Setting up security' / 'Setting up SSH keys' / 'GitHub SSH auth works' lines came out merged on one line, padded to terminal width; a second run of the same code printed cleanly. Suspect: github-ssh-status runs ssh with stdin still on the TTY, or a terminal reflow artifact.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run juliet-bootstrap -y in a narrow (~100 col) cmux pane
2. Resize the pane wider before capturing the scrollback
3. Compare the 'Setting up security' lines in the capture
acceptance_criteria:
- Root cause identified with evidence
- Either a code fix lands, or the bead is closed as a terminal reflow artifact with that evidence recorded
close_reason: Not a script bug. Reproduced the security step's ssh probe under script(1): output bytes are clean (\r\n per line, no stray CR/escapes) and stty modes are unchanged before/after. The merged line in the scrollback is padded to the terminal width, which is what soft-wrapped rows look like when they're re-joined. The prompt rule widened from ~83 to ~180 cols between the two runs (the window was resized), and the second run of the same code printed cleanly. So it was a cmux/terminal reflow artifact. No code change.
